clue.text: Get help, we hear, with the answer — it's conducive to sobriety

parts.note: from the old British catchphrase 'the answer's a lemon', meaning a flat refusal or a useless reply

indicators.note: we hear tells us a word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken, not as it is written

parts.note: help means aid, assistance

explanation.surface: Someone seeking support and an answer is steered towards a soft drink that keeps them sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns AID into its sound-alike ADE. 'The answer's a lemon' is an old British saying for a dismissive non-answer, which is why 'the answer' gives LEMON.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft drink contains no alcohol, so drinking it is conducive to staying sober.

clue.text: Transplanted maple here for short term gain

indicators.note: transplanted suggests things dug up and set down elsewhere, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone moves a maple tree to this spot hoping for a quick benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transplanted' rearranges MAPLE HERE; 'for' and 'gain' only round off the surface, which pretends the definition is about quick profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting only a brief while is fleeting, existing for just a short time.

clue.text: Man of property, three quarters in gold

indicators.note: in tells us the quarters are placed inside the word for gold

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
three of the four quarters of the compass: west, north and east, W N E

explanation.surface: A rich man holds three-quarters of his wealth in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three quarters' looks like a fraction of something, but it is three compass points, W, N and E, set inside OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of property is one who possesses land or goods, a holder of title to them.

clue.text: Fit to take over

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means suitable or fitting; as a verb it means to seize or take possession of something for one's own use.

clue.text: Call in the president — it leads to a solution

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, ignoring the breaks between them

explanation.surface: Bring in the head of state, since that will lead to a resolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call in' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'Call' alone is the definition and 'in' points into 'president — it leads'.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone something is to give them a name or title, to designate them.

clue.text: Veer wildly from the point and wait outside

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for wait goes around the compass point

parts.note: to wait at table is to serve
W, west, is one of the points of the compass

explanation.surface: A driver lurches away from the target and then sits waiting outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word; 'the point' is a compass point, W, placed inside SERVE by 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve is to change direction suddenly and sharply, a wild sideways veer.

clue.text: Hard to place

explanation.definitionFit: Concrete or jelly that has set is firm and solid; to set something down is to put or position it.

clue.text: Running away from work, in principle

indicators.note: in tells us the word for work is placed within the word for principle

parts.note: an element is a basic principle, as in the elements of a subject
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone skips their job on a point of principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word. OP is a standard shortening of opus, a musical or literary work.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloping is running away secretly to marry, usually without parental consent.

clue.text: Love for fine art — not quite an admirable quality

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short of completion, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a virtue is a morally admirable quality

explanation.surface: A passion for fine art is almost, but not entirely, a moral merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtu is a taste or love for curios and objets d'art, connoisseurship of fine things.

clue.text: Parade-ground language to avoid

explanation.definitionFit: A drill sergeant's clipped bark of 'attention' comes out as one short syllable; as a verb it means to keep away from or reject.

clue.text: Biscuits supplied in small numbers

parts.note: petit is French for small
fours are numbers, as in several fours

explanation.surface: Biscuits are served in modest quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplied in' is link. The pieces are the French word for small and a plural of a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Petits fours are tiny fancy cakes or biscuits served after a meal.

clue.text: Beginning of growth — more by accident?

indicators.note: by accident suggests things thrown together haphazardly, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A question of whether new life mostly begins by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by accident' rearranges MORE BY; 'by' in the fodder and 'by' in the indicator are two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: An unborn creature in its earliest stage of development is the start of an organism's growth.

clue.text: Refined tenor first, then a flute's playing

parts.note: T is a standard abbreviation for tenor in music

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being moved about as notes are, so the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician of good taste brings the tenor in first and then a flute plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first, then' only orders the pieces: T leads, followed by the rearranged A FLUTES.
explanation.definitionFit: A refined person shows good taste and discernment in style or manners.

clue.text: Payments to be made by local communities

explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is a sum paid to resolve a debt or claim, and also a small village or colony where people have settled.

clue.text: Promotion to first team don't opt for women!

parts.note: not choosing women amounts to choosing men instead, prefer men

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word team

explanation.surface: A selector picking the first eleven is warned against choosing female players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't opt for women' must be read in reverse: choosing not women is choosing men, PREFER MEN. 'first team' gives T, set at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Preferment is advancement to a higher rank or office, a step up.

clue.text: Fast Rolls-Royce due for overhaul. But he'll take you for a ride

definitions.text: he'll take you for a ride

indicators.note: for overhaul suggests the parts are taken apart and rebuilt, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: RR is the familiar badge abbreviation for Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A speedy luxury car needs servicing, and its seller is a con man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for overhaul' rearranges FAST, RR and DUE. 'take you for a ride' sounds like a car journey, but it is the idiom for cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler cheats people; to take someone for a ride is to deceive them.

clue.text: Cryptaesthesia, in brief, you begin to perceive

parts.note: cryptaesthesia is extrasensory perception, shortened to ESP

indicators.note: begin points to the opening letter of the word you

explanation.surface: With a short burst of second sight, you start to sense things.
explanation.walkthrough: Cryptaesthesia is a rare word for perception beyond the normal senses, so 'in brief' asks for its standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of or notice something, to see it.

clue.text: I'm not poor, thanks to upgrading

definitions.text: I'm not poor, thanks to upgrading

indicators.note: upgrading suggests something being reworked and improved, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says a step up the ladder has lifted them out of poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upgrading' rearranges I'M NOT POOR, and the whole clue describes the rise that made the speaker comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Advancement to a higher job brings more pay, which is how the speaker stopped being poor.

clue.text: Prison isle from which only the fit return

indicators.note: return means the word comes back the other way, so it is read backwards

parts.note: fit people are able, healthy enough to do things

explanation.surface: An island jail that only the healthy ever come back from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses ABLE. The island is where Napoleon was exiled in 1814, a prison of sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was banished to this Mediterranean island, which served as his place of confinement.

clue.text: Jack requiring emulsion for discharge

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, AB for able seaman
an emulsion is a liquid mixture, loosely a solution

explanation.surface: A decorator named Jack needs emulsion paint to finish a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name; it is the crossword sailor, AB. 'requiring' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is release from guilt or sin, a formal discharge from penalty.

clue.text: Mercenary to work at Billingsgate, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us the phrase is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: Billingsgate is London's wholesale fish market, so working there means to sell fish

explanation.surface: A hired soldier takes a job down at the fish market.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate is London's famous fish market. Working there is to SELL FISH, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercenary person acts only out of self-interest and desire for money.

clue.text: A lot may be meant by the satisfactory transaction

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a large amount, as in a great quantity, and also a bargain or favourable exchange.

clue.text: There's nothing vague about universal abhorrence

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: about means the word for vague goes round the letter for universal

parts.note: dim means vague or indistinct, as in a dim memory
U is the film classification for universal

explanation.surface: Nothing is uncertain about a hatred that everyone shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'universal abhorrence' reads as one phrase, but 'universal' gives U, which 'about' places inside DIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or disgust directed at someone, strong loathing.

clue.text: One is lucky to make a thousand at the race-course

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: A punter at the races hopes to win a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a famous English racecourse. 'to make' and 'at' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object thought to bring good luck.

clue.text: Jump — though not to a conclusion

definitions.text: Jump — though not to a conclusion

parts.words: Jump — though not to a conclusion
parts.note: a sudden jolt of surprise, which is also the opposite of a conclusion, the beginning, rather than the hasty leap of jumping to conclusions

explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on 'jump to a conclusion': the word wanted means a jump, and also means the very opposite of a conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A start is a sudden involuntary jump of surprise, and also a beginning, the reverse of an end.

clue.text: Strain from place below causing a blow-up?

indicators.note: from places the word for strain after the underworld it comes from

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, the place below
strain means tension

explanation.surface: Stress from underground pressure is making something explode.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and his realm, so 'place below' is Hades. 'blow-up' looks like an explosion; it is a swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Distension is swelling or enlargement, the way a balloon is inflated by pressure.

clue.text: You get nothing in changing a pound

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters are swapped about into a new order

parts.note: L, from the Latin libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: Converting a pound leaves you with no money at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges IN with L, the pound sign's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil means zero, as in a football score.

clue.text: Spotted deer; a number returning

indicators.note: returning means the word comes back the other way, so it is read backwards

parts.note: six is a number

explanation.surface: Several dotted deer come back to the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses SIX to give XIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The axis or chital is an Asian deer with a white-spotted coat.

clue.text: Unprincipled to spread alarm about nothing

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the letter for nothing
to spread something is to scatter it about, so the letters of alarm are rearranged

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: It is unscrupulous to stir up panic over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges ALARM into AMRAL, and 'about' wraps it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoral person lacks any moral sense, without principles of right and wrong.

clue.text: Expressing doubts about the saint

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone voices misgivings regarding a holy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'concerning', but it rearranges THE SAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hesitant is unsure and wavering, voicing uncertainty.
